title: 429. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Solving Trigonometric Equations on Restricted Intervals
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Sine equation on the first quadrant
questions.learningObjective: Solve a sine equation when the interval is restricted to acute angles.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\) with \(0^\circ\le x\le 90^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The equation has the solutions \(30^\circ\) and \(150^\circ\) in one full turn, but only \(30^\circ\) lies in the interval \(0^\circ\le x\le 90^\circ\). The value \(150^\circ\) must be rejected because it is greater than \(90^\circ\).
questions.hint: Solve the equation, then keep only the solutions that lie in the stated interval.

questions.concept: Cosine equation on a half turn
questions.learningObjective: Solve a cosine equation when the interval is half a turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\cos x=0\) with \(0\le x\le\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The cosine is \(0\) at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) in one full turn. Only \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) lies in \([0,\pi]\), because \(\frac{3\pi}{2}>\pi\).
questions.hint: List the solutions in one full turn, then compare each with the endpoints of the interval.

questions.concept: Sine equation on the second quadrant
questions.learningObjective: Select the solution of a sine equation that lies in a given quadrant interval.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\sin x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) with \(\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\pi\)?
questions.explanation: In one full turn the solutions are \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{3\pi}{4}\). The interval \(\left[\frac{\pi}{2},\pi\right]\) is Quadrant II, which contains \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) but not \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
questions.hint: Find the solution whose terminal side lies in the quadrant described by the interval.

questions.concept: Cosine equation on the lower half turn
questions.learningObjective: Select the solution of a cosine equation in the second half of a turn.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\cos x=-\frac{1}{2}\) with \(\pi\le x\le 2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: In one full turn the solutions are \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) and \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), with reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) in Quadrants II and III. Only \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) satisfies \(\pi\le x\le 2\pi\).
questions.hint: Cosine is negative in two quadrants; decide which of them lies in the interval.

questions.concept: Tangent equation on the lower half turn
questions.learningObjective: Select the solution of a tangent equation in the second half of a turn.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\tan x=1\) with \(\pi\le x\le 2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The solutions of \(\tan x=1\) are \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}+k\pi\). Taking \(k=1\) gives \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\), which lies in \([\pi,2\pi]\). The value \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) is less than \(\pi\), and \(k=2\) gives \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\), which is greater than \(2\pi\).
questions.hint: Write the general solution and test consecutive integer values of \(k\).

questions.concept: Sine equation on the principal interval
questions.learningObjective: Solve a sine equation on an interval that requires a negative angle.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\sin x=-\frac{1}{2}\) with \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: Sine is odd, so \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=-\frac{1}{2}\), and \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) lies in the interval. The angle \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\) also has sine \(-\frac{1}{2}\), but it is greater than \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and is therefore excluded.
questions.hint: In this interval a negative sine must come from a negative angle.

questions.concept: Counting solutions on a longer interval
questions.learningObjective: Count the solutions of a sine equation on an interval longer than one period.
questions.question: How many solutions does \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\) have with \(0\le x\le 3\pi\)?
questions.explanation: In \([0,2\pi)\) the solutions are \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\). Adding \(2\pi\) gives \(\frac{13\pi}{6}\) and \(\frac{17\pi}{6}\), and both are at most \(3\pi=\frac{18\pi}{6}\). So there are four solutions in \([0,3\pi]\).
questions.hint: After finding the solutions in the first period, add \(2\pi\) and check which new values are still in the interval.

questions.concept: Cosine equation on a negative interval
questions.learningObjective: Solve a cosine equation on an open interval of negative angles.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\cos x=\frac{1}{2}\) with \(-\pi<x<0\)?
questions.explanation: Cosine is even, so \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}\), and \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) lies between \(-\pi\) and \(0\). The value \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) is positive, so it is outside the interval.
questions.hint: Use \(\cos(-x)=\cos x\) to find a negative angle with the same cosine.

questions.learningObjective: Take endpoint exclusion into account when solving on an open interval.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sin x=0\) with \(0<x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The sine is \(0\) at every multiple of \(\pi\). The strict inequalities \(0<x<2\pi\) exclude the endpoints \(0\) and \(2\pi\), so the only solution in the open interval is \(x=\pi\).
questions.hint: Check whether the inequality signs include or exclude the endpoints.

questions.concept: Tangent equation on a symmetric interval
questions.learningObjective: Solve a tangent equation on an interval containing negative and positive angles.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\tan x=\sqrt{3}\) with \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The general solution is \(x=\frac{\pi}{3}+k\pi\). For \(k=0\) this is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), and for \(k=-1\) it is \(\frac{\pi}{3}-\pi=-\frac{2\pi}{3}\); both lie in \([-\pi,\pi]\). For \(k=1\) the value \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) is greater than \(\pi\), so it is excluded.
questions.hint: Use the general solution and try negative as well as positive integers \(k\).
